subject.title: feat(mcp-apps): support bounded model context updates

question: Should OpenClaw permit a live MCP App View to inject up to 16 KiB of non-transcript text into the next normal user turn without user-visible approval or disclosure?
rationale: The upstream protocol permits hosts to supply and optionally display this context, but whether OpenClaw should expose the invisible prompt-influence channel is a product and security-boundary choice rather than a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Accept the MCP App trust boundary
options.body: Approve the bounded, live-view-only context channel as an intentional capability, with clear documentation that trusted MCP Apps may influence the next turn.

options.title: Require user-visible disclosure
options.body: Keep the capability but add a host-level indication or approval flow before pending App context is attached to a user turn.

options.title: Pause the capability
options.body: Do not expose update-model-context until maintainers define a broader policy for App-originated hidden model context.

recommendation.title: Accept the MCP App trust boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the bounded, live-view-only context channel as an intentional capability, with clear documentation that trusted MCP Apps may influence the next turn.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently landed adjacent MCP App lifecycle work and are best placed to explain the intended host trust model and implementation boundary.
